def-qftx-physical-bps-index.physical_scope: A selected physical supersymmetric Hilbert-space sector with pure-point spectrum and trace-class heat operators. It asserts no continuum QFT construction, universal BPS count, empirical observation, or existence of a state in nature.

def-qftx-physical-bps-index:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. A **pure-point physical index datum** consists of a specified physical model record and its operator data. The model record identifies the spacetime and spatial domain, metric and orientation, global gauge group including its global form, field bundles and representations, adopted action or other postulates, and boundary conditions; it also states whether the Hilbert-space operators are constructed directly or obtained from a named regulator and measure. These are supplied model inputs, not conclusions of this definition. When curved spacetime is used, the record includes fixed Riemannian spin geometry, spin and R-symmetry data, and the model-specific spinor equation as in the earlier background definition; no claim is made that arbitrary geometry admits such data. The operator data include a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^+\oplus\mathcal H^-$ as an orthogonal sum of closed subspaces, and the grading operator $\Gamma$ equal to $+I$ on $\mathcal H^+$ and $-I$ on $\mathcal H^-$. They supply a densely defined self-adjoint operator $\mathcal Q$ with domain invariant under $\Gamma$ and $\mathcal Q\Gamma\psi=-\Gamma\mathcal Q\psi$ on that domain. Set $K=\mathcal Q^2$ on $D(K)=\{\psi\in D(\mathcal Q):\mathcal Q\psi\in D(\mathcal Q)\}$ and require that $K$ is nonnegative and self-adjoint. The grading is dimensionless; if $K$ has energy units, $\mathcal Q$ has energy dimension $1/2$.

Require an orthogonal pure-point decomposition

$$\mathcal H=\mathcal H_0^+\oplus\mathcal H_0^-\oplus\widehat{\bigoplus}_{\lambda\in\Sigma}(\mathcal H_\lambda^+\oplus\mathcal H_\lambda^-),$$

where $\Sigma\subset(0,\infty)$ is a supplied countable set of distinct eigenvalues, $\mathcal H_0^\pm=\ker K\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ are finite-dimensional, and each $\mathcal H_\lambda^\pm=\ker(K-\lambda I)\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ is finite-dimensional and contained in $D(K)$. A compatible orthonormal basis $E=E^+\sqcup E^-$ of these subspaces is supplied as part of the data. For each $\beta>0$, also supply a bounded diagonal operator $T_\beta$ with eigenvalue $1$ on $E\cap\ker K$ and $e^{-\beta\lambda}$ on $E\cap(\mathcal H_\lambda^+\oplus\mathcal H_\lambda^-)$, and require $T_\beta$ to be trace class. The parameter $\beta$ has units of inverse energy when $K$ has energy units; in dimensionless radial-quantization conventions it is dimensionless.

The **Witten index** of this datum is the absolutely convergent graded heat supertrace, defined by the supplied basis rather than by an unproved basis-independence claim,

$$W_E(\beta)=\sum_{e\in E^+}\langle T_\beta e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in E^-}\langle T_\beta e,e\rangle,\qquad \beta>0,$$

where each heat operator is trace class, meaning compact with summable singular values, and the supplied-basis diagonal sums are absolutely convergent; the sums are taken over finite subsets and then their absolutely convergent limits. This signed supertrace is not a raw state degeneracy. The zero-gap subspace singled out by the selected supercharge is $\ker K=\mathcal H_0^+\oplus\mathcal H_0^-$. Equality of the full heat supertrace with the even-minus-odd dimension of this subspace is a separate conditional theorem under the exact hypotheses. A physical model may call this a **BPS index** only when its own supercharge algebra identifies this kernel with a specified BPS-saturated sector. Here a BPS-saturated state means a domain vector in a specified massive rest fiber satisfying the mass/central-charge equality in the earlier BPS definition. The present definition does not identify every BPS state with $\ker K$ and asserts no such state exists.

def-qftx-superconformal-index.physical_scope: A trace-class Hilbert-space representation of the specified four-dimensional N=1 superconformal charge sector on the unit round S3. It asserts no general SCFT construction, convergence outside the declared fugacity domain, continuum path-integral identity, or empirical claim.

def-qftx-superconformal-index:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $S^3=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:|x|=1\}$ have its round metric and standard orientation. The **radial Hilbert space** $\mathcal H_{S^3}$ is the complex Hilbert space supplied by the chosen physical model after quantization on this unit spatial three-sphere; its construction is model input, not proved here. The model record names its gauge group and global form, matter representations, action or other adopted postulates, and the Hilbert-space construction or regulator and measure; the spatial sphere has no boundary, and any other boundary or domain conditions are stated as input. The rotation group is $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=SU(2)_1\times SU(2)_2$. Let $E$ be the dimensionless self-adjoint conformal Hamiltonian, $J_1,J_2$ the self-adjoint Cartan generators of the two rotation factors, and $R$ the self-adjoint $U(1)_R$ charge. Normalize $R$ so that the chosen right-handed Poincare supercharge $Q=\widetilde Q_{\dot -}$ has $R$-charge $+1$ and $J_2$-weight $-\tfrac12$; it has $J_1$-weight zero. Its actual Hilbert adjoint in radial quantization is the conformal supercharge $Q^\dagger=\widetilde S^{\dot -}$. The model supplies a common invariant dense product domain, an even grading $\Gamma=(-1)^F$ with $Q$ and $Q^\dagger$ odd, $Q^2=(Q^\dagger)^2=0$, and the exact positive self-adjoint operator relation

$$\Delta=\frac12\{Q,Q^\dagger\}=E-2J_2-\frac32R\ge0.$$

The protected sector is $\ker\Delta=\ker Q\cap\ker Q^\dagger$, since on the common domain $\langle\Delta\psi,\psi\rangle=\tfrac12(\|Q\psi\|^2+\|Q^\dagger\psi\|^2)$. Define the two dimensionless commuting charges

$$J_+=J_1+J_2+\frac12R,\qquad J_-=J_2-J_1+\frac12R.$$

Also require the odd operator $\mathsf Q=(Q+Q^\dagger)/\sqrt2$ on its stated domain to be self-adjoint and to satisfy $\mathsf Q^2=\Delta$ as a closed-operator equality. Supply a simultaneous pure-point decomposition for $\Delta,J_+,J_-$ and $\Gamma$, with a compatible orthonormal Hilbert basis $E=E^+\sqcup E^-$. More explicitly, the basis vectors have real charge eigenvalues $(\lambda,a,b)$, with $\lambda\ge0$, and span the joint subspaces $\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}^\pm$; the distinct joint labels form a supplied countable set. Each closed self-adjoint charge has its maximal diagonal domain: for eigenvalues $d_e$ its domain consists of the coefficient sequences $\psi=\sum_e c_e e$ with $\sum_e|d_e c_e|^2<\infty$. This specifies the joint spectral calculus, not merely formal commutators on test vectors. The total eigenspaces of $\Delta$, including positive ones, may be infinite-dimensional.

For every joint charge projection $P_{\lambda,a,b}$, require reducing-domain commutation with the closed supercharges: $P_{\lambda,a,b}D(T)\subset D(T)$ and $TP_{\lambda,a,b}\psi=P_{\lambda,a,b}T\psi$ for $T=Q,Q^\dagger,\mathsf Q$ and $\psi\in D(T)$. The grading preserves these subspaces and anticommutes with the odd operators on their domains. Thus the given commuting fugacity charges preserve the actual closed supercharge domains and the finite-span joint eigenvector domain; no integrated spectral conclusion is inferred from a common-domain commutator alone.

For positive real fugacities $p,q\in(0,1)$, define $\Xi_{p,q}=p^{J_+}q^{J_-}$ by the supplied joint diagonal calculus, with eigenvalue $p^a q^b$ and its maximal diagonal domain. Define $T_{\beta,p,q}$ first on the finite span of $E$ by $T_{\beta,p,q}e=p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}e$. An admissible pair is one for which this positive diagonal operator extends to a bounded trace-class operator for every dimensionless $\beta>0$; denote that extension by $\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}$. This notation specifies the closed diagonal product, without assuming that an arbitrary product of unbounded operators is everywhere defined. Its supplied-basis diagonal sum is then absolutely convergent. Every joint charge block is finite-dimensional for an admissible pair: its common eigenvalue $p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}$ is strictly positive, so infinitely many orthonormal vectors of that weight would contradict trace-class summability. Infinitely many joint blocks, an infinite protected kernel, and infinite total multiplicity at fixed $\lambda$ are allowed. The **right-handed four-dimensional N=1 superconformal index** is

$$\mathcal I_R(p,q;\beta)=\sum_{e\in E^+}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in E^-}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}e,e\rangle,$$

where $E=E^+\sqcup E^-$ is the supplied joint energy/charge/parity eigenbasis. The positive supercharge gap singles out $\ker\Delta$ as the protected sector, with signed fugacity weight $\Xi_{p,q}$; equality of the full heat supertrace with a trace over that sector is a separate conditional theorem. Other supercharges or central-charge sectors are not silently included. If the weighted trace-class or absolute-convergence condition fails, the expression is only a formal series until a separate regularization and its validity are supplied. No analytic convergence is asserted for all $p,q\in(0,1)$.

pthm-qftx-physical-index-beta-independen.physical_scope: Conditional operator-theoretic deduction for a selected physical Witten-index datum with pure-point spectrum, finite zero eigenspaces, and trace-class heat operators. It asserts no continuum QFT construction, regularized trace identity, empirical claim, or universal BPS-state count.

pthm-qftx-physical-index-beta-independen:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. A physical application supplies its spacetime and spatial domain, global gauge group and global form, field bundles and representations, adopted action or other postulates, boundary conditions, and either a Hamiltonian/Hilbert construction or the regulator and measure used to produce its operator data. The conclusion is conditional on those inputs yielding the following exact data. Let $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^+\oplus\mathcal H^-$ be a complex Hilbert space with grading $\Gamma=+I$ on $\mathcal H^+$ and $-I$ on $\mathcal H^-$. Let $\mathsf Q$ be a densely defined self-adjoint odd operator with $\Gamma$-invariant domain, and let $K=\mathsf Q^2$ be nonnegative and self-adjoint on its composition domain. Assume an orthogonal pure-point decomposition

$$\mathcal H=\mathcal H_0^+\oplus\mathcal H_0^-\oplus\widehat{\bigoplus}_{\lambda\in\Sigma}(\mathcal H_\lambda^+\oplus\mathcal H_\lambda^-),$$

where $\Sigma\subset(0,\infty)$ is countable, each parity eigenspace $\mathcal H_\lambda^\pm=\ker(K-\lambda I)\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ is finite-dimensional and contained in $D(K)$, $\mathcal H_0^\pm=\ker K\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ is finite-dimensional, and the union of compatible orthonormal bases is a Hilbert basis. Assume $e^{-\beta K}$ is trace class for each $\beta>0$. Then the physical Witten index defined by the supplied basis is

$$W_E(\beta)=\sum_{e\in E^+}\langle e^{-\beta K}e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in E^-}\langle e^{-\beta K}e,e\rangle=\dim\mathcal H_0^+-\dim\mathcal H_0^-$$

for every $\beta>0$. The conclusion concerns only this discrete trace-class operator datum; it does not assert a continuous-spectrum cancellation, a validity theorem for a regulator, a continuum limit, or an identification of the kernel with every physical BPS state.

pthm-qftx-superconformal-index-beta-inde.physical_scope: Conditional result for the specified unit-radius four-dimensional N=1 charge data with a supplied pure-point joint gap/charge basis, reducing supercharge domains, and trace-class weighted heat operators; total gap eigenspaces and the protected kernel may be infinite-dimensional. It asserts no continuum measure, general SCFT existence, or formal-series regularization theorem.

pthm-qftx-superconformal-index-beta-inde:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and take the exact right-handed four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal operator data on the unit round $S^3$ specified in the earlier definition. In particular, $\mathsf Q=(Q+Q^\dagger)/\sqrt2$ is self-adjoint and odd, $\Delta=\mathsf Q^2\ge0$, and the model supplies the simultaneous pure-point energy/charge/parity basis and reducing-domain projection identities in that definition. Neither the protected kernel nor a total positive-gap eigenspace is required to be finite-dimensional. For an admissible $0<p,q<1$, $\Xi_{p,q}=p^{J_+}q^{J_-}$ has eigenvalue $p^a q^b$ on each joint block $\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}$, and the diagonal products $T_{\beta,p,q}=\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}$ extend to bounded trace-class operators for all $\beta>0$. Then

$$\mathcal I_R(p,q;\beta)=\sum_{e\in E_0^+}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in E_0^-}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e,e\rangle$$

for all $\beta>0$, where $E_0^\pm$ are supplied compatible orthonormal bases of $\ker\Delta\cap\mathcal H^\pm$. The zero-sector sums converge absolutely even when the protected kernel is infinite-dimensional, and the superconformal index is independent of $\beta$. No assertion is made for continuous spectrum, a nonconvergent formal trace, or an unproved regularization.

ex-qftx-witten-index-finite-superpartner.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional supersymmetric quantum-mechanical Hilbert-space example with exact discrete trace. It is not a continuum QFT, an observed system, or a claim about a naturally realized particle.

ex-qftx-superconformal-index-free-chiral.physical_scope: A conditional free, ungauged four-dimensional N=1 protected-letter/Fock trace on unit S3 with the explicit charge and convergence data stated here. It is not a continuum construction, gauge-projected index, empirical observation, or universal formula for interacting theories.
